## 2. Population and Methods

The primary population is `is_first_attempt == True`: one sitting per delivered
candidate, independently checked against chronological history and supplied attempt
number. Form A and Form B are analyzed separately; no cross-form score or item
pooling is used. Membership comes from item metadata (AB plus the sitting's form),
not item-name patterns. There are 60 scored items per sitting. The 20 common
designated anchors each receive one set of statistics per form. First attempt means
first observed within the supplied window; earlier external history is unavailable.

Correct=1, incorrect=0 and omitted administered=0, with the denominator equal to
all administered candidates for that item/form. There are 194 omissions in
the primary response records; structurally absent items never enter a matrix.
Difficulty is n_correct/n_administered with a 95% Wilson interval, z=1.959963984540054.
Intervals are itemwise, not simultaneous, and assume independent first candidates.
Corrected discrimination is Pearson corr(X_j, total-X_j); the focal item is always
excluded. Constant items, constant rest scores and insufficient observations return
undefined (CSV empty numerical cells plus explicit status), never zero.

Reliability uses sample variance (ddof=1): alpha=k/(k-1) times
[1-sum(s_j²)/s_total²]. For KR-20, each pq is multiplied by n/(n-1) before division
by sample total variance. This is equivalent to conventional KR-20 with population
total variance and ensures exact agreement with alpha up to rounding. Deletion
alpha recomputes the (k-1)-item rest-score variance and uses (k-1)/(k-2), rather than
retaining the original total variance. Values are not clipped into [0,1].

Alpha intervals use 2000 candidate-row resamples with
replacement within each form and percentile endpoints 2.5%/97.5%. Rows are ordered
by administration_id. Seeds are 20261021 for A and
20261022 for B (NumPy default_rng). The number of valid/undefined
replicates is reported; draws are retained. Each primary candidate appears once.
Secondary all-administration results contain repeated candidates and are
**descriptive only**, with no Wilson intervals, alpha intervals or bootstrap.
Neither retake rows nor form samples are treated as independent for uncertainty
in that secondary analysis.

Exploratory difficulty screens use p<0.2 and
p>0.9. Discrimination screens are r<0 (priority),
0≤r<0.2 (low),
0.2≤r<0.3 (attention),
and r≥0.3 (generally acceptable screening).
These configurable cutoffs are not universal quality standards. Configuration was
specified before viewing Stage 2 results and was not tuned to obtain a finding count.
STAGE2_CONFIG.json and analysis_config.json record the adopted rules.

## 3. Binary Item Data and Missingness

Observed correct/incorrect marked responses become 1/0. Administered omissions are
NaN in the latent response matrix, not silently counted as observed incorrect.
Structurally not-administered items never enter a form matrix. The primary method
is all-60-item complete cases, producing the retained samples above; every pair in
a primary form therefore has the same N. Original scores and Stage 1/2 datasets are
unchanged. No latent responses are imputed.

These score summaries are observed unadjusted selection descriptions, not a test

the represented population; omission causes remain unavailable. Exported first-
attempt matrices preserve missing cells, and analysis matrices record the exact
retained administration/candidate IDs and item order.

Sensitivity 1 excludes only prespecified ANC_14 on the **same full-form complete
cases**, avoiding confounding an item exclusion with recovered candidates.
Sensitivity 2 includes all first attempts and treats operational omissions as zero.
This changes both response coding and candidate retention; it cannot isolate the
two effects. No other item exclusions or rekeying were explored.

## 4. Correlation Matrix Diagnostics

Primary association estimates are two-step tetrachorics: marginal thresholds are
estimated from the observed 2×2 table and the bivariate-normal joint probability is
inverted for rho. The implementation uses a deterministic Plackett integral with
the transformation t=sin(theta), 32-node
Gauss–Legendre quadrature, doubled-node verification and safeguarded Newton steps.
Adaptive quadrature plus Brent inversion is a documented fallback. It does not
assume a package tetrachoric API or use a randomized bivariate CDF.

For a table with any zero cell, 0.5 is
added to **all four cells**, then marginal thresholds are recalculated. Positive
cells below 5 are flagged as sparse but
not automatically adjusted. Constant margins are unidentifiable and are not
artificially rescued by continuity correction. Pair-level raw cells, N, correction,
iterations, error checks, fallback method and convergence status are retained.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 1015 | 1015 | 1015 | -0.1243 | 279.5604 | 1 | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| B | 957 | 957 | 957 | 0.0157 | 1132.9216 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Symmetry and unit diagonals are checked, item order is preserved, and all raw
matrices remain available. The condition number is the singular-value condition
number, so a finite value does not establish positive definiteness. Pearson/phi
matrices are separately labeled descriptive sensitivity evidence, not substitutes
for tetrachoric latent association estimates.

When the smallest tetrachoric eigenvalue is below 1e-6, EFA uses a **separate copy**
conditioned by Higham PSD/unit-diagonal alternating projections with Dykstra
correction, followed by a 1e-6 eigenvalue floor and diagonal rescaling. Prespecified
numerical safeguards require convergence, maximum correlation change ≤0.05 and
relative Frobenius change ≤0.05; these are not universal psychometric standards.
Unsupported conditioning would withhold EFA rather than silently replace evidence.

not evidence that the raw matrix was already a valid population correlation matrix.
**Raw tetrachorics are used for scree and parallel analysis; only EFA uses any
conditioned copy.** No automatic modification is made to prior data or item keys.

## 5. Eigenvalue and Parallel Analysis Evidence

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

These are component eigenvalues of correlation matrices (PCA-style evidence), not
common-factor explained variance. The first root's fraction of the unit-diagonal
trace is not an estimate of common-factor variance explained. Negative raw roots
indicate sample matrix inadmissibility; they are not negative latent variances.
The Kaiser greater-than-one rule is not the sole or primary decision criterion.

Parallel analysis independently permutes each observed binary column, preserving
its exact correct-count marginal and the analysis N. Missing positions, if present,
are fixed; the chosen complete-case/zero specifications are complete binary matrices.
Reference matrices use the **same raw tetrachoric estimator and continuity rule**
as the observed matrix. No continuous-normal reference and no mixed Pearson/
tetrachoric eigenvalue comparison is used.

Each of six form/specification analyses uses 100 valid
Monte Carlo references and the 95th percentile at each
ordered root. Seeds are 20261023 + 1000×form_index +
100×specification_index (A=0, B=1; specifications in the sensitivity table's order).
The computational pilot and exact seeds are saved. The rule retains the leading
consecutive roots above their order-matched reference percentile, stopping at the
first nonexceedance. Nonconsecutive pointwise exceedances remain visible but do not
silently add retained dimensions. Null matrices need not be PD to yield diagnostic
raw eigenvalues; all pairs must converge for a reference to count as valid.

Parallel analysis suggests a dimensional count relative to this null, not proof
of the true latent dimension count. Fixed marginals and finite N influence the
reference distribution. First ten roots and reference percentiles are plotted
with a secondary-root detail panel.

Primary models use every first observed sitting and all available observed item
responses; complete cases are not required. Correct=1, observed incorrect=0,
administered omissions=missing. Structural nonmembers are absent from that form's
matrix. Missing cells contribute no Bernoulli term. All original observations and
operational scores are preserved; operational omissions still earn zero under the
unchanged 42/60 scoring rule.

Ignoring the missingness mechanism assumes it is ignorable for item-parameter
inference conditional on the modeled observed-response/proficiency structure,
with separable mechanism parameters. This is a modeling assumption, not an
empirical finding that omissions are MCAR/MAR or unrelated to competence. Omission
causes and timeout/completion status remain unavailable. Sensitivity models score
omissions zero on the **same first-attempt candidates**, isolating coding from the
complete-case selection difference present in Stage 3. The 59-item sensitivity
excludes only ANC_14 and retains the same candidates. No retakes enter calibration.

## 4. Model and Identification

P(X_ij=1|theta_i)=logistic(d_j+a_j theta_i), logistic scaling D=1. Slopes a_j may be
positive, zero or negative. The intercept d_j is estimated directly. The crossing
location b_j=-d_j/a_j is reported only if |a_j|≥0.1
and a model-based slope interval is available and excludes zero. Otherwise b is
undefined/unstable, not a huge printed value. For a negative slope, b is a decreasing
curve's P=0.5 location, not ordinary increasing-item difficulty.

Each form and specification independently fixes theta~Normal(0,1). Global reflection
is resolved by requiring positive aggregate item discrimination, aligning theta with
the dominant positively discriminating pattern. This never flips an individual
item's response coding. Common items are separately estimated; they impose no
linking constraints. Numerical theta/b/information values between forms are not
automatically equivalent. Even within-form sensitivity contrasts are conditional
on a shared standardized identification convention, not a linking result.

## 5. Estimation and Numerical Diagnostics

Marginal maximum likelihood integrates candidate likelihoods with standard-normal
Gauss–Hermite quadrature. Initial estimation used 31 nodes and was checked at 41.
The initial EAP mean absolute differences slightly exceeded the declared 0.01
tolerance; this result is retained. Resolution was increased without relaxing the
criterion: reported models use 81 nodes and are
checked against 101. Original 31/41 calibrations and
their failed resolution checks remain visible. Stable log-logistic probabilities and
log-sum-exp integration avoid overflow/underflow. L-BFGS-B optimizes mean negative
marginal log-likelihood with analytic gradients from two deterministic starts;
quadrature/zero sensitivities also use the corresponding primary solution as one
start. The best converged likelihood is retained by a prespecified rule; every
start and failure is logged, not selected for favorable substantive findings.

The slope safeguards are ±6.0 and intercept
safeguards ±10.0; they are not plausibility
targets. All boundary hits are reported. Per-candidate projected maximum gradient
must be ≤1e-06 in addition
to optimizer success. Bounds, tolerances, iterations, warnings and quadrature are
saved. No minimum positive slope is imposed.

## 4. Residual Correlation Methodology

r_ij=X_ij-P_j(EAP_i). Raw Q3 is the Pearson correlation between two residual columns
using pair-specific observed subsets and centering. At least two paired values and
positive residual variance are required; undefined correlations remain unavailable,
not zero. Adjusted Q3 subtracts the **unweighted mean across unique finite
off-diagonal pairs within the same form/specification**. Means are not pooled across forms.
No unavailable primary correlations occurred.

EAP uses the same responses, including focal items. Finite-test shrinkage and this
reuse can bias Q3 even under local independence. Adjustment does not remove every
item-specific bias. Reference simulations reproduce the exact EAP/residual/centering
procedure. A generic .20 or .30 cutoff is not a significance threshold.
The need for context-specific Q3 references and mean adjustment is supported by
[Christensen, Makransky and Horton (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1177/0146621616677520).
Their Rasch findings motivate a fitted-design reference here; no Rasch cutoff is
transferred to this signed 2PL analysis.

## 5. Parametric Null Reference

Each form first completed 5 pilot replicates with
separate deterministic seeds, then targeted 500 valid main
replicates (maximum 550 attempts). For each attempt:
draw new independent theta~N(0,1), draw independent Bernoulli responses conditional
on theta and the fixed signed calibration, restore the exact observed missing mask,
recalculate EAP using 81 nodes, then recalculate raw/adjusted Q3 and its maximum
positive adjusted value. Every attempted replicate, numerical failure and seed is logged.

| form | phase | seed | completed_valid | attempted | numerical_failures | elapsed_seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | pilot | 20261025 | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0.0812 |
| B | pilot | 20261026 | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0.0972 |
| A | main | 20261125 | 500 | 500 | 0 | 11.1885 |
| B | main | 20261126 | 500 | 500 | 0 | 8.4607 |

SeedSequence([form_seed, attempt_index]) identifies independent reproducible draws.
The paired-value arrays and item ordering are retained in compressed NPZ files,
together with the missing mask and raw-Q3 mean. Raw pair draws can be reconstructed
as adjusted draw plus that replicate's mean. Pilot draws do not enter thresholds.
Each pair's own null mean, SD, lower/upper quantiles and exceedance counts are in
q3_pointwise_reference.csv and the full pair table.

Family-wise 95%/99% thresholds use the corresponding quantiles of the **maximum
positive adjusted Q3 over all 1,770 pairs**, separately by form. The fixed `higher`
order-statistic rule and strict observed > threshold comparison were set before
examining results. No cross-form 3,540-pair error-control claim is made. Nested flags
and exclusive classifications distinguish 99%, 95%-only, pointwise-only and no
notable positive association. Pointwise screening is exploratory, without multiplicity control.

Empirical tail areas use (1 + number of reference values >= observed)/(B+1), so the
smallest attainable value is 1/(B+1), never zero. With B=500 the resolution is
0.001996; only about five reference draws inform the upper 1% tail. Binomial
tail-proportion SEs at .05/.01 are approximately .00975/.00445; these are Monte
Carlo limitations, not parameter-confidence intervals. Quantile method, counts,
tail areas and numerical failures are exported. Marginal near-threshold classifications
can move with additional simulation, and no formal certainty is claimed.

This is a **fixed-calibration parametric reference**, not a full refitting bootstrap.
It omits fitted-item uncertainty and assumes the fitted latent distribution and
ignorable, fixed omission pattern. A refitting sensitivity is a later recommendation.

reference controls screening across the within-form family under the adopted

of shared content, copying, scoring errors or defective items. Lack of a flag is
not proof of local independence or adequate power, particularly for small effects.

whole-person deletion. Every item records regression N and group/outcome counts.

## 4. Matching Strategy

For every target j, compute the 81-node posterior mean using the fixed Stage 4 full
60-item signed calibration and only available responses in the selected matching
pool, excluding j and ANC_14. If j=ANC_14, focal exclusion leaves 59 matching items;
other primary targets use 58. Negative target discrimination is retained and ANC_14
remains eligible for testing. Fixed parameters were originally fitted on the same
sample and may themselves be contaminated by DIF. Focal exclusion does not prove
an invariant matching set or independently observed proficiency.

Each item's rest EAP is centered over all matching-eligible first-attempt candidates
in that form, including candidates whose target response is omitted. The same
center is used for both groups and every nested model. At least one observed
matching item is necessary; prior-only posteriors are not treated as measured ability.
Matching centers, posterior SDs, exact pools, IDs, target masks and values are archived.

## 5. Primary Logistic DIF Models

M0: logit(P)=beta0+beta1*T. M1 adds beta2*G. M2 adds beta3*T*G.
Each triplet uses exactly the same target-specific response rows; an observation-ID
hash is retained with every fit and test. Uniform support is M0–M1 (1 df), nonuniform
increment M1–M2 (1 df), and primary omnibus M0–M2 (2 df). Components support
interpretation after the omnibus screen; they are not independent discovery routes.
This model distinction follows [Swaminathan and Rogers (1990)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1745-3984.1990.tb00754.x).

Unpenalized ML uses deterministic Newton/IRLS with analytic gradient/information and
Armijo backtracking. RMS design-column scaling aids computation; coefficients and
covariances are transformed back to centered matching units. Convergence requires
maximum scaled gradient/N ≤1e-08,
with at most 100 iterations. Full rank, positive
information and condition number below 10000000000.0
are required for supported ordinary ML inference.

A linear program searches for a nonzero direction with nonnegative signed margins;
a max-min-margin program distinguishes complete from quasi-complete separation.
Separated, rank-deficient, failed or unstable fits receive unavailable coefficients,
SEs and tests. The prespecified fallback is to withhold ordinary ML inference;
no penalized/Firth estimates are substituted into ordinary likelihood-ratio tests.
All statuses, iterations, gradients, condition numbers and failures remain visible.

## 6. Multiplicity and Effect Sizes

BH at q=.05 is applied to 60 omnibus tests per form. Unavailable tests retain their
prespecified family slots conservatively as p=1 for adjustment, with unavailable
q-values returned as unavailable. A separate BH family of all 120 primary form-item
tests is a cross-form multiplicity sensitivity, not pooled calibration. The rule
and q threshold were set before results. Supplementary methods/passes retain their
own within-form BH bookkeeping and do not replace the primary discovery family.
BH relies on its usual null-dependence conditions; correlated tests and estimated
matching limit literal guarantees. No executive finding rests only on unadjusted p.

Coefficient SEs and 95% Wald intervals use supported observed information. M1's
North/South odds ratio is additive-model-specific. M2's group coefficient is the
contrast at centered T=0; with interaction, group odds vary with T and no constant
OR summarizes the entire effect. Probabilities and North−South differences are
shown across supported locations, with pointwise delta-method uncertainty from
the full M2 coefficient covariance. These bands omit matching/item uncertainty
and are not simultaneous confidence bands or independent validation.

Nagelkerke R²(M)=[1−exp(2(LL_null−LL_M)/N)]/[1−exp(2 LL_null/N)], using the intercept-only
target model on identical observations. Incremental R² is R²(M2)−R²(M0); additive
and interaction increments are also retained. Integrated signed mean differences
describe direction; integrated absolute differences preserve crossing effects.
Directional contrasts at supported q10/q50/q90 and the supported-grid maximum
absolute difference are exported. No universal practical-effect cutoff is imposed.

## 4. Reference Proficiency Population

The primary reference is N(0,1) on the Form A metric, applied identically to both forms. Secondary references are the B identification distribution transformed onto A, N(shift_B,scale_A²), and an equal-weight mixture 0.5×N(0,1)+0.5×N(shift_B,scale_A²). A mixture is integrated component by component, not replaced by a moment-matched single normal. `reference_population_definitions.csv` and the saved conditional quadrature arrays specify every scenario.

These are imposed, model-based identification scenarios. They do not establish empirical population distributions, equivalent candidate groups, random assignment or population-invariant equating. No relationship formed from different reference populations for the two forms is labeled common-population equating.

## 5. Conditional and Marginal Score Distributions

Lord–Wingersky recursion begins with f_0(0)=1 and adds each Bernoulli item: f_j(s)=(1−p_j)f_(j−1)(s)+p_j f_(j−1)(s−1). Signed, zero and near-zero item slopes affect response probabilities without invalidating the recursion. All 61 probabilities (scores 0–60) are saved for each integration node. No negative-probability clipping, probability renormalization or empirical smoothing is used. Conditional means equal the TCC and conditional variances equal Σp(1−p). Marginal means and variances are checked independently against integration and the law of total variance.

The true/observed distinction and recursive approach follow [Lord & Wingersky's primary ETS report](https://www.ets.org/research/policy_research_reports/publications/report/1983/ihpw.html); recursion and marginalization are also documented in [Huang & Cai (2021)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11336-021-09785-y). The implementation here is the unidimensional Bernoulli algorithm, not their multidimensional extension.

Deterministic Gauss–Hermite integration starts at 81 nodes per normal component and tests 161, then 321 and 641 if necessary. Criteria were fixed before results: maximum PMF difference ≤1e−8, maximum central mapping difference ≤0.001 score and maximum inverse A38–46 mapping difference ≤0.0001. All 12 point scenarios required 321 nodes: 81→161 did not meet the stringent PMF tolerance; 161→321 passed. Failed lower-resolution comparisons are preserved, not relabeled successful. Calibration remains the original 81-node fit; integration resolution is a separate numerical choice.

## 7. IRT Observed-Score Equating

The declared research convention uses F(s)=P(S≤s) and integer mid-percentile R(s)=F(s)−0.5×P(S=s), expressed as a proportion from 0 to 1. Between integer scores R is linearly interpolated; B→A is inverse_R_A(R_B(s)). Lower and upper cumulative tails are evaluated separately to reduce cancellation. Exact flat percentile intervals yield a nonunique status and no numerical mapping. Values outside the reference integer-score mid-percentile range are unavailable: no extrapolation or silent clipping to 0/60 occurs. This explicit mid-CDF interpolation is the chosen discrete convention, not a claim that all equipercentile conventions coincide.

Continuous estimates remain fractional research correspondences. Floor, nearest integer with halves rounded upward, and ceiling interpretations are saved separately. They do not turn a fractional estimate into an observed score. The complete 0–60 technical CSV includes percentiles, method, anchor set, common reference, support and uncertainty status. It is not an approved conversion table and is not reproduced as such in this executive report.

Central research support requires source mid-percentile between 0.025 and 0.975 and the TCC locations of both corresponding numerical scores within the fixed Stage 7 central theta overlap.
